chapter: New Orleans bands after the war
title: After the war: Young Olympia, Young Tuxedo and Bob Lyons bands
summary: Alexis worked twice with the Young Olympia, then the Young Tuxedo band (Celestin's overflow), then Bob Lyons' band replacing Willie Edwards, and recalls its members.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well you came back from the war and you say then you worked with the Young Olympia first, didn't you?
Young Olympia band twice. Then the Young Tuxedo band, which Doc Oynos the bass player was the band. Freddie Babu was the trombone player.
Well I want to ask a little bit about that name, Young Tuxedo.
They worked on the Celestan. Everything Celestan couldn't handle he'd give it to us. You understand?
So it wasn't a rival band exactly then. They weren't trying to cash in on the name of the Tuxedo album. Oh no, no.

Celestan used to send us on jobs and things. Called the original Tuxedo and the Young Tuxedo. That's what the name was. I played with them. So it was wild. When I left them I joined Bob Lyons band. When I took Willie Edwards place.
You got his in the Bob Lyons band.
Yeah. Didn't get all the members of the Bob Lyons band. You have the trumpet and who was clarinet? Sidney Bean. That's right. Sidney Bean.

When he was a skeleton trombone. Yes indeed. Yes I worked with him with Bob Lyons band. He worked with us with Bob Lyons band. August Rousseau. He had a mommy shop uptown years ago. Was he a Routiner or what? Was he a Routiner or a reader? He could read. Yeah. Nice old man.
Did he have a play with someone? Yeah. Did he have a play with someone?
Did he have a play with someone? Did he have a play with someone? Did he have a play with someone? Did he have a play with someone?
Did he have a play with someone?
Did he have a play with someone? Nice old man.
Did he ever play with songs then?
He did. He played on the street. He was afraid.
